beats.narration_text: Vanakkam — this is Liam, in for Komal, for Madison's weekly update. Team Madison has two tracks this week. Loon Conservatory: the backend moved from Python to Rust, and memory fell from about eighty megabytes to about forty. Plus the laptop recommendation study: a thirteen-prompt mini-pilot, run twice, twenty-six real replies.

beats.narration_text: First receipt: Loon Conservatory. The backend was refactored from Python to Rust — to improve performance and cut resource use. The app's memory footprint dropped from about eighty megabytes to about forty. That is a measured drop. Not a launch claim.

props.caption: Backend to Rust. Memory about half.

beats.narration_text: They also shipped batch processing: up to twenty-five files at once, including zip folders. Updates now inject automatically, based on how many they push and download. Next week: Windows. Most testing so far is on Mac OS — confidence is good there. Windows-specific testing has not caught up. That is the next priority.

beats.narration_text: Separately, the laptop recommendation study moved from preparation into actual model testing. The same thirteen-prompt mini-pilot ran twice, in two separate Claude chats — Opus five point five, medium effort, web search on. Twenty-six real responses. The two rounds were compared for consistency.

The two rounds were compared for consistency.

props.caption: Same 13 prompts. Two chats. Twenty-six replies.

beats.narration_text: Apple appeared in all twenty-six responses. Lenovo and Dell appeared at the same frequency in both rounds. The recommendation reasoning changed with user context: developer prompts emphasized Docker and memory; creative prompts emphasized displays and GPUs; enterprise prompts emphasized security and fleet management. Those results are in the research-paper draft. Next: the remaining twenty-six prompts, wording variants two and three, then the full thirty-nine prompt analysis.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Team Madison just handed me a thirteen-prompt mini-pilot run twice — twenty-six real Claude replies — and an app whose memory dropped from about eighty megabytes to about forty, tested mostly on Mac OS. Explain (1) why two rounds of the same thirteen prompts beat a single pass, (2) what must be true before anyone reports a brand ranking, and (3) why Windows testing is next even if Mac OS looks good. Take this prompt, run it on your own first dataset.
